k: There is a cup of water at her feet. It is still cool.
src: 'There is a cup of water at her feet. It is still cool.'

k: Water
src: 'Water'

k: Saltglass is east... but that smoke in the north. Someone could be hurt out there.
src: 'Saltglass is east... but that smoke in the north. Someone could be hurt out there.'

k: Lift-glass housing
src: 'Lift-glass housing'

k: The mainmast. Someone has carved a tally into it — dozens of little marks — and, at the top, a single word: STAY.
src: 'The mainmast. Someone has carved a tally into it — dozens of little marks — and, at the top, a single word: STAY.'

k: The foremast, splintered halfway up. A torn sail flaps from it like a flag of surrender. Or a very tired wave.
src: 'The foremast, splintered halfway up. A torn sail flaps from it like a flag of surrender. Or a very tired wave.'

k: Cargo crates stamped with a dozen different port seals. Half of them are empty. The other half are labeled "DEFINITELY NOT CONTRABAND."
src: 'Cargo crates stamped with a dozen different port seals. Half of them are empty. The other half are labeled "DEFINITELY NOT CONTRABAND."'

k: GREYSPINE PASS — Frosthollow, a day's climb.nWALK SOFTLY. THE SNOW LISTENS.
src: 'GREYSPINE PASS — Frosthollow, a day\'s climb.\nWALK SOFTLY. THE SNOW LISTENS.'

k: QUIET WAY. Do not run. Do not shout.nDo not sing, Brother Tolle.
src: 'QUIET WAY. Do not run. Do not shout.\nDo not sing, Brother Tolle.'

k: QUIET WAY. The snow above has been waiting all winter. Do not give it a reason.
src: 'QUIET WAY. The snow above has been waiting all winter. Do not give it a reason.'

k: Resting my knees. They're older than the rest of me.
src: 'Resting my knees. They\'re older than the rest of me.'

k: Gray cloaks passed me on the lower trail two days ago. Forty of them, with a big man in front who never looked at the view.
src: 'Gray cloaks passed me on the lower trail two days ago. Forty of them, with a big man in front who never looked at the view.'

k: Who climbs a mountain and doesn't look at the view?
src: 'Who climbs a mountain and doesn\'t look at the view?'

k: Vigil Stone
src: 'Vigil Stone'

k: Frozen pack
src: 'Frozen pack'

k: A shrine to the Keepers of Frosthollow. Pilgrims have tied strips of cloth to it — prayers, names, a child's mitten.
src: 'A shrine to the Keepers of Frosthollow. Pilgrims have tied strips of cloth to it — prayers, names, a child\'s mitten.'

k: Frost lily
src: 'Frost lily'

k: FROSTHOLLOW. Pilgrims welcome. Beds free.nThe goats are not for petting. (They bite.)
src: 'FROSTHOLLOW. Pilgrims welcome. Beds free.\nThe goats are not for petting. (They bite.)'

k: Came up for the Keeper's blessing. Stayed for the soup.
src: 'Came up for the Keeper\'s blessing. Stayed for the soup.'

k: There's an army camped at the foot of the mountain. Sunburst banners. Holy soldiers, I thought — but I watched them a whole evening, and they never once prayed.
src: 'There\'s an army camped at the foot of the mountain. Sunburst banners. Holy soldiers, I thought — but I watched them a whole evening, and they never once prayed.'

k: Sweep, sweep. I keep sweeping the steps to the tower.
src: 'Sweep, sweep. I keep sweeping the steps to the tower.'

k: Nobody climbs them now. I sweep them anyway. Somebody should keep the way clear.
src: 'Nobody climbs them now. I sweep them anyway. Somebody should keep the way clear.'

k: Snow, snow, snow. Sweep, sweep, sweep.
src: 'Snow, snow, snow. Sweep, sweep, sweep.'

k: The mountain is very generous with its snow. I am very generous with my broom. We have an understanding.
src: 'The mountain is very generous with its snow. I am very generous with my broom. We have an understanding.'

k: Run, Halloway. It's what Keepers' children are good at.
src: 'Run, Halloway. It\'s what Keepers\' children are good at.'

k: The Bell Stair, Wren! GO!
src: 'The Bell Stair, Wren! GO!'

k: Bell tower
src: 'Bell tower'

k: The well is frozen over. Someone has chipped a hole in the ice and left a ladle beside it, the way you'd leave a key under a mat.
src: 'The well is frozen over. Someone has chipped a hole in the ice and left a ladle beside it, the way you\'d leave a key under a mat.'

k: Gate road's crawling with gray cloaks, sparrow. Wrong way.
src: 'Gate road\'s crawling with gray cloaks, sparrow. Wrong way.'

k: The Ice Score
src: 'The Ice Score'

k: I keep airing the beds. Tolle would want them aired.
src: 'I keep airing the beds. Tolle would want them aired.'

k: He wrote from Saltglass. Two pages about the children and one line about himself: "I am managing." He underlined "managing." That boy.
src: 'He wrote from Saltglass. Two pages about the children and one line about himself: "I am managing." He underlined "managing." That boy.'

k: A guest book. Three winters back, in a big looping hand: "Sir Aldous Venn and squire. Couldn't sleep. Lovely tea."
src: 'A guest book. Three winters back, in a big looping hand: "Sir Aldous Venn and squire. Couldn\'t sleep. Lovely tea."'

k: Steps cut into the ice by hand, worn down in the middle by centuries of monks' feet. Each step has a number carved beside it. You are on step four hundred and twelve.
src: 'Steps cut into the ice by hand, worn down in the middle by centuries of monks\' feet. Each step has a number carved beside it. You are on step four hundred and twelve.'

k: A little bell is carved into the wall by the Hearthstone, and under it: FOR THE ONES WHO HAD TO LEAVE IN A HURRY.
src: 'A little bell is carved into the wall by the Hearthstone, and under it: FOR THE ONES WHO HAD TO LEAVE IN A HURRY.'

k: Boots on the stair behind us. There's no going back.
src: 'Boots on the stair behind us. There\'s no going back.'

k: SALTGLASS — last sweet water for thirty leagues.nThe Lantern is open to pilgrims from dawn until dusk.nCaravans north: ask at the yard.
src: 'SALTGLASS — last sweet water for thirty leagues.\nThe Lantern is open to pilgrims from dawn until dusk.\nCaravans north: ask at the yard.'

k: Caravan Market! Everything that came across the sand and survived it.
src: 'Caravan Market! Everything that came across the sand and survived it.'

k: Prices are fixed. Fixed by me. Daily. Sometimes hourly.
src: 'Prices are fixed. Fixed by me. Daily. Sometimes hourly.'

k: Caravans
src: 'Caravans'

k: Teo hasn't stopped sulking since your little friend came out of the Lantern glowing.
src: 'Teo hasn\'t stopped sulking since your little friend came out of the Lantern glowing.'

k: Thirty days until his birthday. I'm going to need a bigger sulk-bucket.
src: 'Thirty days until his birthday. I\'m going to need a bigger sulk-bucket.'

k: We walked from Thistledown so my Teo could be Kindled in Saltglass light. His grandfather was. And his grandfather.
src: 'We walked from Thistledown so my Teo could be Kindled in Saltglass light. His grandfather was. And his grandfather.'

k: Now we wait thirty days for his birthday, in a town where water costs more than wine.
src: 'Now we wait thirty days for his birthday, in a town where water costs more than wine.'

k: We're playing Lanterns and Gloam! I'm the Gloam! RAAAH!
src: 'We\'re playing Lanterns and Gloam! I\'m the Gloam! RAAAH!'

k: Rafi is ALWAYS the Gloam. He says the Gloam is the best part.
src: 'Rafi is ALWAYS the Gloam. He says the Gloam is the best part.'

k: The Gloam is NOT the best part. The best part is when the sun comes back.
src: 'The Gloam is NOT the best part. The best part is when the sun comes back.'

k: The children sing on the Lantern steps every morning. The Keeper sits with them.
src: 'The children sing on the Lantern steps every morning. The Keeper sits with them.'

k: She says it's the worst choir she's ever heard. She cried the first time.
src: 'She says it\'s the worst choir she\'s ever heard. She cried the first time.'

k: Yrsa looks up at you and hums three notes of the morning hymn. Then she goes back to drawing a bell in the sand.
src: 'Yrsa looks up at you and hums three notes of the morning hymn. Then she goes back to drawing a bell in the sand.'

k: The deep well of Saltglass. The rope goes down, and down, and down.
src: 'The deep well of Saltglass. The rope goes down, and down, and down.'

k: You drop a pebble. Four heartbeats later, very faintly: _plink._
src: 'You drop a pebble. Four heartbeats later, very faintly: _plink._'

k: Chimes
src: 'Chimes'

k: Master Ruel's furnace. The air above it wobbles like a mirage that can't make up its mind.
src: 'Master Ruel\'s furnace. The air above it wobbles like a mirage that can\'t make up its mind.'

k: The Lamp
src: 'The Lamp'

k: The lamp of Saltglass burns inside a cage of saltglass panes. The light comes out of the glass in every direction at once.
src: 'The lamp of Saltglass burns inside a cage of saltglass panes. The light comes out of the glass in every direction at once.'

k: Up close it hums — low, like a cat that's pleased with itself. Or a cat that isn't.
src: 'Up close it hums — low, like a cat that\'s pleased with itself. Or a cat that isn\'t.'

k: A mirror of polished saltglass. Your reflection is a half-step behind you, as if it's thinking things over.
src: 'A mirror of polished saltglass. Your reflection is a half-step behind you, as if it\'s thinking things over.'

k: A mirror of polished saltglass. In it, the Lantern's light looks like dawn. In the room, it looks like noon.
src: 'A mirror of polished saltglass. In it, the Lantern\'s light looks like dawn. In the room, it looks like noon.'

k: A cool bed, a cold supper, and a jug of real water? Sixty gold. The water alone is worth forty.
src: 'A cool bed, a cold supper, and a jug of real water? Sixty gold. The water alone is worth forty.'

k: the Cool Well
src: 'the Cool Well'

k: The Hierophant's men used to ride through and bless the wells.
src: 'The Hierophant\'s men used to ride through and bless the wells.'

k: Now they ride through and _count_ them. Why would you count wells? Wells don't go anywhere.
src: 'Now they ride through and _count_ them. Why would you count wells? Wells don\'t go anywhere.'

k: ...Unless you expect to need every one of them.
src: '...Unless you expect to need every one of them.'

k: I'm writing a ballad about the Sunscar. So far it rhymes "sand" with "sand" eleven times.
src: 'I\'m writing a ballad about the Sunscar. So far it rhymes "sand" with "sand" eleven times.'

k: Critics call it "accurate."
src: 'Critics call it "accurate."'

k: I used to run the salt road in four days. Now I walk to the well and back and call it a day's work.
src: 'I used to run the salt road in four days. Now I walk to the well and back and call it a day\'s work.'

k: Best days of my life, then and now. Only now's got Nim in it.
src: 'Best days of my life, then and now. Only now\'s got Nim in it.'

k: Papa came home! He was SO dirty. Mama made him take two baths.
src: 'Papa came home! He was SO dirty. Mama made him take two baths.'

k: I drew you a picture. It's you, and the big one, and the girl with black hair, and the little one with the Crest. The little one is the biggest because he asked.
src: 'I drew you a picture. It\'s you, and the big one, and the girl with black hair, and the little one with the Crest. The little one is the biggest because he asked.'

k: A shelf of maps — salt roads, caravan wells, wind patterns — all annotated in a quick, slanted hand. "J." in every corner.
src: 'A shelf of maps — salt roads, caravan wells, wind patterns — all annotated in a quick, slanted hand. "J." in every corner.'

k: Can you— is there a way through? Please. Please, I have a daughter.
src: 'Can you— is there a way through? Please. Please, I have a daughter.'
